title: The 8 Levels of Planning a Fake Dream Trip
house: A bustling fruit-and-vegetable metropolis named Produce City, where towering skyscrapers made of giant hollowed-out gourds cast long shadows over neon-lit asphalt streets, and every single resident wears a glowing digital forehead display of their monthly disposable income.
catchphrase: The number on your forehead never lies.
links: The bitter lemon barista in Level 1 mentions a quiet wealthy carrot customer who always tips in gold coins.
The coconut travel agent in Level 3 spots the broke strawberry running past her agency window.
The dragon fruit influencer in Level 6 complains about a loud orange making flight videos on public transit.

gegenspieler.tat: Laughs loudly at her handwritten itinerary and spills expensive imported oat milk over her printed map.

levels.name: Milo, 22, Grocery Bagger
levels.story: The 8 levels of planning a luxury vacation with zero budget. Level 1. Level 1: 120 dollars a month to plan a first-class trip to Bora Bora. My name is Milo, I'm a sweet potato guy with dirt smudged on my cheeks, and my jacket is safety-pinned together. I'm sitting at the corner table of the neon-lit Central Station Diner, sketching a five-star overwater bungalow on a dirty napkin while my app shows exactly zero cents for flights. You are booking a private yacht with two dollars in your pocket, Milo. Are you swimming across the ocean? The whole diner goes dead silent, staring at my flashing red digit. My face burns hot under the fluorescent lights as I clutch my colored pencils. I pull a crumpled paper stub from my pocket and whisper my exact philosophy right back at her. We are all just tourists passing through a town we cannot afford. Then my phone vibrates violently with a notification that changes everything. You will see that in Level 2. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Cleo, 25, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of planning a luxury vacation with zero budget. Level 2. Level 2: 850 dollars a month and an entire wall covered in postcard dreams of Tokyo. My name is Cleo, a sour lemon person with a permanent bitter frown, working the espresso machine at the commuter rail station kiosk. I spend every spare second measuring flight times with a ruler on a huge world map taped to the tiles. You are measuring first-class routes with barista tips, Cleo? You will never even afford a bus ticket to the suburbs. My yellow peel heats up with pure humiliation as commuters stare at my low number. I grip the steaming milk pitcher and look him dead in the eyes with my sharpest comeback. My imagination flies much faster than your overpriced private jet. Suddenly, a strange courier drops a sealed Manila envelope onto my spill tray. You will see that in Level 3. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Maya, 28, Freelance Illustrator
levels.story: The 8 levels of planning a luxury vacation with zero budget. Level 3. Level 3: 2,100 dollars a month spent entirely on mood boards for a nonexistent trip to the Swiss Alps. My name is Maya, an avocado woman with smooth green skin and a large wooden pit pendant around my neck, sitting cross-legged on my studio floor surrounded by printed hotel brochures. My roommate, a towering coconut man from Level 7 with a hard, hairy brown shell and an 8,900 dollar forehead, kicks my stack of Swiss Alps photos across the hardwood floor. You are building snow castles with freelance table scraps, Maya. You cannot even afford a winter coat, let alone a ski chalet in Zermatt. My green cheeks burn with rage as I scramble to pick up my scattered pictures of snowy peaks. I look up from the floor and deliver the line that makes him pause. A poor artist builds palaces while a rich man lives in a cage. Just as he turns to storm out, my phone lights up with a text from an unknown sender. You will see that in Level 4. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Sam, 31, Junior Accountant
levels.story: The 8 levels of planning a luxury vacation with zero budget. Level 4. Level 4: 4,500 dollars a month spent entirely on planning a fantasy honeymoon to Santorini with no partner in sight. My name is Sam, an orange man with a dimpled citrus texture and wire-rimmed glasses, sitting at my cubicle under harsh fluorescent lights with three different booking tabs open. You are booking sunset cliff villas for two when you eat instant ramen alone, Sam. Even your calculator feels sorry for you. My citrus peel tingles with humiliation as neighboring cubicle workers chuckle softly. I push my glasses up my nose and give her a cold, calculated reality check. I am investing in my happiness while you are only counting everyone else's pennies. Suddenly, the office phone rings with an exclusive travel agency invite. You will see that in Level 5. levels.name: Zoe, 29, Senior Architect
levels.story: The 8 levels of planning a luxury vacation with zero budget. Level 5. Level 5: 7,200 dollars a month and an entire architectural portfolio dedicated to luxury treehouse resorts in Bali. levels.name: Victor, 42, Hedge Fund Director
levels.story: The 8 levels of planning a luxury vacation with zero budget. Level 7. Level 7: 38,000 dollars a month spent on booking private islands in the Pacific just to test internet speeds. My name is Victor, a robust broccoli man with a dense, dark green florets crown and an impeccably tailored pinstripe suit, sitting at the head of a mahogany boardroom table reviewing global vacation portfolios. You are spending millions on imaginary islands while our portfolio is bleeding out, Victor. You are nothing but a loud stalk of stems. A real boss buys the island while the accountant keeps counting the sand. Suddenly, the boardroom double doors fly open, revealing an unexpected visitor with a shocking demand. You will see that in Level 8. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Aura, 50, Master Architect
levels.story: The 8 levels of planning a luxury vacation with zero budget. Level 8. The finale. Level 8: Unlimited numbers on the forehead, yet I live in a modest wooden cabin at the very edge of Produce City. My name is Aura, an ancient coconut-and-pine hybrid woman with silver-dusted roots and an infinite symbol glowing across my forehead where digits used to be. Every single person you saw across all seven levels—Milo the sweet potato, Cleo the bitter lemon, Maya the avocado, Sam the orange, Zoe the dragon fruit, Leo the coconut, and Victor the broccoli—was never planning a real trip. They were all testing their own capacity to dream when reality tried to crush them. I walk down the central avenue of Produce City as the digital signs above us all flicker simultaneously. The sweet potato's debt vanished, the lemon's Tokyo map became a real ticket, and the billionaire's island was shared with everyone. I stop in front of the Central Station Diner where it all started, looking directly into the camera lens. The number on your forehead never lies, but it also never tells you where you are actually going. Now tell us in the comments below: Which topic should we explore in the next series?
